question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Annual death counts show whether the total fatal burden went down, without implying an exposure-adjusted risk.
options.answer: Motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26.4% lower), but this crash file cannot determine whether deaths per mile driven declined because it contains no miles-driven measure.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual count of motorists killed in reported NYC crashes declined: it fell from 110 deaths in 2013 to 81 in 2025, a 26.4% decrease. An annual count is a defensible measure of fatal burden, but it is not a risk rate and can change with travel exposure. The question's per-mile-risk part remains unanswered because the file has no miles-driven denominator. Within 2013–2025, no rows are left out for NULL crash dates or motorist-killed values (0% in each year), and every included year is complete; other years are outside the requested period.

options.denominator: All police-reported crash records in the same calendar year
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by reported crash volume distinguishes fatality burden from changes in the number of crashes, while remaining explicit about the available denominator.
options.answer: Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 53.99 in 2013 to 94.69 in 2025 (75.4% higher), so this crash-based proxy did not decline; per-mile risk is not measurable from these data.
options.interpretation: This framing addresses a crash-normalized proxy for the requested risk: motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes increased from 53.99 in 2013 to 94.69 in 2025, up 75.4%. It is defensible because the denominator controls for yearly police-reported crash volume, but it measures deaths relative to crashes rather than miles driven. Therefore the actual per-mile-risk question remains unanswered because no vehicle-miles-traveled or other miles-driven data are present. Within 2013–2025, no rows are left out for NULL crash dates, motorist-killed values, or crash-count denominators (0% in each year), and every included year is complete; other years are outside the requested period.

answer:
